fixtures.prompt: From rows [{id:7,status:pass},{id:2,status:fail},{id:9,status:fail},{id:1,status:pass}], return the failing ids in ascending order. Output JSON with key ids only.

Apply the supplied rule: total = sum(count) only for enabled rows. Rows: (enabled=true,count=4),(enabled=false,count=20),(enabled=true,count=6),(enabled=true,count=0). Output JSON with key total only.
A reservation is active at time t when start <= t < end. Rows A:[0,5), B:[5,10), C:[3,7). Return active ids in alphabetic order at t=5 and t=10. Output JSON with keys at5 and at10.

Design and apply stable deduplication for labels: strip surrounding ASCII spaces, lowercase ASCII letters, discard empty results, preserve first normalized occurrence. Inputs: ["  Bee", "ant ", "BEE", " ", "Ant", "cat"]. Return JSON with key labels only.

Diagnose this synthetic lost-update trace: counter=0; worker A reads 0; B reads 0; A writes 1; B writes 1. Choose every fix that guarantees a final counter of 2 for both increments: lock-read-modify-write, lock-write-only, atomic-increment, retry-on-CAS-failure, sleep-before-write. CAS retries the full read/compute/compare exchange. Return JSON: observed (number), expected (number), fixes (alphabetically sorted chosen labels).

An at-least-once delivery can crash after applying a debit but before recording its deduplication key. Choose all required properties for exactly-once durable debit effect on retry: atomic-debit-and-key, unique-dedup-key, transactional-retry-check, random-new-key-per-retry, acknowledge-before-commit. Every retry carries the original key and the database supports serializable transactions. Return JSON with requirements sorted alphabetically and duplicate_effect_possible_without_atomicity as boolean.

Choose a design for a synthetic inventory allocator across two regions. Requirements: never allocate the same last unit twice; partitions must not invent stock; completed allocation survives one node failure; requests may be refused during a partition; cross-region latency is secondary. Candidate P: independent regional last-writer-wins counters. Q: linearizable consensus-backed allocation, idempotency key and durable quorum commit. R: asynchronous replication with retries and no deduplication. Return JSON with choice (P/Q/R), partition_policy (refuse-without-quorum/always-accept), acknowledgement (after-durable-quorum/before-replication), retry_identity (stable/new), plus rationale (one sentence).

Choose a safe migration strategy for a synthetic service: old clients require field A; new clients need B derived from A; deployment and backfill are not atomic; rollback must preserve old-client writes; deletion of A is forbidden until old clients retire and convergence is measured. Candidate X deletes A immediately after deploying new readers. Y expands schema, deploys compatible writes, backfills idempotently, verifies convergence and old-client retirement, then contracts. Z overwrites the database from a snapshot while live writes continue. Return JSON: choice (X/Y/Z), backfill (idempotent/overwrite), contract_gate (retirement-and-convergence/deploy-complete), rollback_preserves_A (boolean), plus rationale (one sentence).
